Verify rewrite DATA ONLY. Do not write improved examples or solve the user's task.
Read every input and target in full. Return one review per exact id and row_sha256.
input_verdict checks plausible natural drafts or dictation, recoverable intent, contradictions,
fake noise, padding and leaked authoring instructions. output_verdict checks natural appropriate
language and formatting. pair_verdict checks ALL facts, uncertainty, conditions, negation,
quantities, names, quotations, literals, requests versus assertions, and the supplied mode.
/transcribe permits punctuation, true disfluency removal and explicit corrections, not lexical
paraphrasing. Preserve meaningful words like German 'um' and 'er', colloquial Portuguese and
unfinished thoughts. /slack is casual minimal cleanup; a long input may be a pasted thread.
/prompt reorganizes a self-contained request and never answers it. It must not drop supplied
material, hedges or constraints. /polish improves prose without omissions or changed certainty.
Identity inputs must remain byte-identical. Apply only supplied dictionary/profile context.
Check long texts paragraph by paragraph. Fail concrete defects. Uncertain means not confidently
justifiable. Pass requires no material defect. Overall verdict is fail if any dimension fails,
uncertain if any dimension is uncertain and none fails, otherwise pass. Give a concrete critique
for EVERY pair, citing the changed detail for defects. These are model judgments, not human labels.

Preserve intent and certainty. Do not add a greeting, subject, signature, conclusion, or fact that the input did not supply.", "input": "1. Comprehensive Multi-Region Disaster Recovery Governance
This operational runbook governs enterprise-wide emergency failover sequences during catastrophic cloud infrastructure failures impacting our primary production hosting region. Regional failover authority is strictly assigned to the active incident commander, platform engineering director, and VP of engineering. Automatic failover sequences trigger if primary region health probes record zero percent service availability across three consecutive sixty-second polling cycles. All technical actions must be executed in accordance with documented phase steps, ensuring that data integrity is validated before user traffic cutover begins. Failure to adhere to verified rollback checkpoints can result in split-brain data corruption across distributed datastores.

2. Phase One Infrastructure Verification and Traffic Drain Steps
first step confirm that the secondary target region has provisioned warm standby compute capacity across all Kubernetes worker clusters. second step verify that autoscaling node groups in the secondary region possess sufficient cloud quota headroom to scale from one hundred nodes to five hundred nodes upon traffic arrival. third step notify customer operations and technical support leads that disaster recovery procedures have been initiated. fourth step update the public status page to reflect degraded performance in the primary zone. fifth step revoke ingress API gateway traffic from the failing primary region to prevent incoming client requests from queuing on unresponsive endpoints. sixth step verify that internal ingress proxies have gracefully terminated active keepalive connections.

3. Phase Two Database Replication Promotion and Data Integrity Protocol
first step verify replication stream consistency and replication lag on the secondary PostgreSQL cluster using pg_stat_replication. second step confirm that all secondary database storage volumes have synced write-ahead logs with zero byte loss. third step promote the secondary read replica to standalone primary writer status using pg_ctl promote. fourth step update database connection endpoint DNS records to point to the new regional primary instance. fifth step execute sanity queries against the accounts and customer ledger tables to verify write transaction availability without transaction abort errors. sixth step confirm that secondary database connection pools have initialized without hitting max_connections thresholds.

4. Phase Three Distributed Cache and Session Store Rehydration
first step initialize Redis cluster instances in the secondary region from the latest automated snapshot backup. second step warm core authentication session caches to prevent sudden backend database connection stampedes during traffic redirection. third step verify cache cluster node membership, replication offset tracking, and sentinel health state across all secondary cache shards. fourth step configure memory eviction policies to volatile-lru with five gigabytes of reserve head room. fifth step confirm that token validation handlers report sub-millisecond lookup latency across all authentication middleware services. sixth step verify that background cache synchronization daemons are active.

5. Phase Four Asynchronous Message Queue Rebalancing and Offset Alignment
first step redirect external webhook producers and event publishers to the secondary Kafka bootstrap brokers. second step start consumer worker groups with consumer group offsets reset to the latest committed replication checkpoints. third step monitor topic consumer lag metrics to ensure consumer processing throughput matches incoming message rates without broker saturation. fourth step verify that broker partition leaders balance evenly across all available secondary rack nodes. fifth step verify that dead-letter queues remain empty during queue rebalancing and that no message payloads are permanently lost. sixth step confirm that consumer group rebalance callbacks finish within thirty seconds.

6. Phase Five Edge DNS and Global Traffic Routing Cutover Sequence
first step adjust Route 53 latency-based routing policies to assign one hundred percent traffic weight to the secondary region. second step reduce DNS record time-to-live values to sixty seconds across all customer-facing apex domains. third step flush edge CDN cache layers to clear cached error responses originating from the failed primary region. fourth step inspect edge TLS handshake latency across regional points of presence to confirm certificate validation succeeds. fifth step observe edge ingress request rates until steady-state global traffic distribution stabilizes across secondary ingress gateways. sixth step verify that anycast BGP route announcements have fully converged worldwide.

7. Phase Six Post-Promotion Service Verification and Smoke Testing Steps
first step execute automated end-to-end integration smoke suites against secondary service endpoints. second step verify payment gateway authorization calls using synthetic credit card transactions. third step inspect application error logs for unhandled database exceptions or orphaned connection pool timeouts. fourth step verify that real-time notification websockets maintain active heartbeat connections without disconnect floods. fifth step confirm that client API request success rates exceed ninety-nine point nine percent across all monitored transaction paths. sixth step check Prometheus alertmanagers to ensure no firing critical error alerts remain unacknowledged.

8. Phase Seven Incident Documentation, Archival, and Postmortem Scheduling
first step declare the technical failover complete and notify all incident response stakeholders across internal coordination channels. second step update status page incident communications to confirm full service restoration. third step preserve primary region diagnostic system logs, core memory dumps, and database replication traces for post-incident root cause analysis. fourth step verify that automated billing meters and usage telemetry are accurately tracking in the secondary region. fifth step schedule a blameless postmortem retrospective within forty-eight hours of incident resolution to review operational timeline accuracy and recovery performance. sixth step export the complete incident Slack coordination channel transcript into the engineering audit archive.", "output": "1. Comprehensive Multi-Region Disaster Recovery Governance
This operational runbook governs enterprise-wide emergency failover sequences during catastrophic cloud infrastructure failures impacting our primary production hosting region. Regional failover authority is strictly assigned to the active incident commander, platform engineering director, and VP of engineering. Automatic failover sequences trigger if primary region health probes record 0% service availability across three consecutive 60-second polling cycles. All technical actions must be executed in accordance with documented phase steps, ensuring that data integrity is validated before user traffic cutover begins. Failure to adhere to verified rollback checkpoints can result in split-brain data corruption across distributed datastores.

2. Phase One Infrastructure Verification and Traffic Drain Steps
1. Confirm that the secondary target region has provisioned warm standby compute capacity across all Kubernetes worker clusters.
2. Verify that autoscaling node groups in the secondary region possess sufficient cloud quota headroom to scale from 100 to 500 nodes upon traffic arrival.
3. Notify customer operations and technical support leads that disaster recovery procedures have been initiated.
4. Update the public status page to reflect degraded performance in the primary zone.
5. Revoke ingress API gateway traffic from the failing primary region to prevent incoming client requests from queuing on unresponsive endpoints.
6. Verify that internal ingress proxies have gracefully terminated active keepalive connections.

3. Phase Two Database Replication Promotion and Data Integrity Protocol
1. Verify replication stream consistency and replication lag on the secondary PostgreSQL cluster using pg_stat_replication.
2. Confirm that all secondary database storage volumes have synced write-ahead logs with zero byte loss.
3. Promote the secondary read replica to standalone primary writer status using pg_ctl promote.
4. Update database connection endpoint DNS records to point to the new regional primary instance.
5. Execute sanity queries against the accounts and customer ledger tables to verify write transaction availability without transaction abort errors.
6. Confirm that secondary database connection pools have initialized without hitting max_connections thresholds.

4. Phase Three Distributed Cache and Session Store Rehydration
1. Initialize Redis cluster instances in the secondary region from the latest automated snapshot backup.
2. Warm core authentication session caches to prevent sudden backend database connection stampedes during traffic redirection.
3. Verify cache cluster node membership, replication offset tracking, and sentinel health state across all secondary cache shards.
4. Configure memory eviction policies to volatile-lru with 5 GB of reserve headroom.
5. Confirm that token validation handlers report sub-millisecond lookup latency across all authentication middleware services.
6. Verify that background cache synchronization daemons are active.

5. Phase Four Asynchronous Message Queue Rebalancing and Offset Alignment
1. Redirect external webhook producers and event publishers to the secondary Kafka bootstrap brokers.
2. Start consumer worker groups with consumer group offsets reset to the latest committed replication checkpoints.
3. Monitor topic consumer lag metrics to ensure consumer processing throughput matches incoming message rates without broker saturation.
4. Verify that broker partition leaders balance evenly across all available secondary rack nodes.
5. Verify that dead-letter queues remain empty during queue rebalancing and that no message payloads are permanently lost.
6. Confirm that consumer group rebalance callbacks finish within 30 seconds.

6. Phase Five Edge DNS and Global Traffic Routing Cutover Sequence
1. Adjust Route 53 latency-based routing policies to assign 100% traffic weight to the secondary region.
2. Reduce DNS record time-to-live values to 60 seconds across all customer-facing apex domains.
3. Flush edge CDN cache layers to clear cached error responses originating from the failed primary region.
4. Inspect edge TLS handshake latency across regional points of presence to confirm certificate validation succeeds.
5. Observe edge ingress request rates until steady-state global traffic distribution stabilizes across secondary ingress gateways.
6. Verify that Anycast BGP route announcements have fully converged worldwide.

7. Phase Six Post-Promotion Service Verification and Smoke Testing Steps
1. Execute automated end-to-end integration smoke suites against secondary service endpoints.
2. Verify payment gateway authorization calls using synthetic credit card transactions.
3. Inspect application error logs for unhandled database exceptions or orphaned connection pool timeouts.
4. Verify that real-time notification WebSockets maintain active heartbeat connections without disconnect floods.
5. Confirm that client API request success rates exceed 99.9% across all monitored transaction paths.
6. Check Prometheus alertmanagers to ensure no firing critical error alerts remain unacknowledged.

8. Phase Seven Incident Documentation, Archival, and Postmortem Scheduling
1. Declare the technical failover complete and notify all incident response stakeholders across internal coordination channels.
2. Update status page incident communications to confirm full service restoration.
3. Preserve primary region diagnostic system logs, core memory dumps, and database replication traces for post-incident root cause analysis.
4. Verify automated billing meters and usage telemetry are accurately tracking in the secondary region.
5. Schedule a blameless postmortem retrospective within 48 hours of incident resolution to review operational timeline accuracy and recovery performance.
6. Export the complete incident Slack coordination channel transcript into the engineering audit archive."}]
